items.stem: Per the UHDDS, how is the principal diagnosis defined?

options.text: The condition established after study to be chiefly responsible for the admission
options.rationale: Correct: this is the UHDDS definition of principal diagnosis.

options.text: The most expensive condition to treat
options.rationale: Cost does not define the principal diagnosis.

options.text: The condition the patient complains about most
options.rationale: The chief complaint is not necessarily the principal diagnosis.

options.text: The last condition documented in the chart
options.rationale: Position in the chart does not determine the principal diagnosis.

items.explanation: Correct: this is the UHDDS definition of principal diagnosis.

PCS codes are seven characters, not five.
PCS codes are seven characters, not ten.

items.stem: Select TWO statements that correctly describe present-on-admission (POA) reporting.

options.text: POA indicates whether a condition was present when the inpatient admission occurred
options.rationale: Correct: POA captures conditions present at the time of admission.

options.text: POA assignment must be supported by provider documentation
options.rationale: Correct: POA indicators must be based on the documented record.

options.text: POA should be assigned to maximize the DRG regardless of documentation
options.rationale: POA must reflect documentation, not reimbursement goals.

options.text: POA applies only to the principal procedure
options.rationale: POA applies to diagnoses, not procedures.

options.text: POA is optional and never affects reporting
options.rationale: POA reporting is required and can affect payment.

items.explanation: Correct: POA captures conditions present at the time of admission. Correct: POA indicators must be based on the documented record.
